# QS-CFW-6417-61 - Quality specification - bearing ring CFW-6417-61 (52100)
Revision: Rev B  
Plant: P1  
Parts: CFW-6417-61

Scope
This quality specification governs acceptance criteria, inspection methods, and nonconformance handling for bearing ring CFW-6417-61 manufactured from material grade 52100 at Plant P1. It applies to forged rings delivered to machining and assembly and to in-process forgings held for inspection prior to heat treatment or finishing. The intent is to ensure functional hardness, dimensional accuracy of the bore, and compliance with forging weight limits for safe handling and traceability.

Requirements table
The table below lists mandatory acceptance criteria that constitute final quality requirements for CFW-6417-61.

- Part identification: CFW-6417-61
- Material: 52100
- Hardness: The hardness range for bearing ring CFW-6417-61 (CFW-6417-61) is 29-35 HRC.
- Bore diameter tolerance: The bore diameter tolerance for bearing ring CFW-6417-61 (CFW-6417-61) is ±0.07 mm.
- Maximum forging weight: The maximum forging weight for bearing ring CFW-6417-61 (CFW-6417-61) is 9.4 kg.
- Visual and surface: Forgings must be free of cracks, laps, and other discontinuities that could impair machining or performance. Light scale and surface oxides are acceptable provided they are removed in subsequent operations without loss of nominal material.
- Identification and traceability: Each forging must be marked or tagged to allow linkage to the associated heat lot and inspection record through the plant document control system.

Inspection method
General approach
Inspectors shall verify requirements listed in the requirements table at designated inspection points: incoming inspection for received forgings, in-process inspection post-forge and pre-heat treatment, and final inspection after finishing operations that affect the bore or hardness. Record results on the part inspection record and file with the part history record for the heat lot.

Hardness verification
Hardness shall be measured using a calibrated portable Rockwell hardness tester set for HRC scale. Measurement locations shall be on the forged surface and representative of the ring wall without crossing machined areas. Take multiple measurements distributed circumferentially and axially to represent variability. Document each reading on the part inspection record and calculate the range observed; the hardness values must be within the specified range above. If readings cluster near either limit, perform additional measurements and attach notes describing locations sampled and any anomalies.

Bore diameter verification
Measure the bore using a calibrated bore gauge or inside micrometer suitable for the part geometry. Ensure the gauge contacts clean, representative surfaces and that measurements are taken at multiple angular positions and along the axial length to detect taper and out-of-round conditions. Record each measurement on the part inspection record. The bore diameter tolerance for bearing ring CFW-6417-61 (CFW-6417-61) is ±0.07 mm; acceptance requires all relevant measurements to be within that tolerance relative to the nominal diameter on the manufacturing drawing.

Weight verification
Weigh forgings on a calibrated scale to confirm they do not exceed the allowed forging mass. The maximum forging weight for bearing ring CFW-6417-61 (CFW-6417-61) is 9.4 kg. Record the weight on the part inspection record. If the weight is below expected nominal mass due to excessive flash removal or other causes, document and investigate for potential missing material.

Sampling and frequency
For lot-based inspection, select samples per the plant sampling plan and for critical features perform 100 percent inspection as directed by the part family risk assessment for this product class. For single-piece releases, perform full verification of all listed requirements on each piece.

Instrument calibration and acceptance
Use instruments with valid calibration status. Attach instrument identifiers and calibration dates to the inspection record. Reject readings from instruments found out of calibration and repeat measurements with a calibrated instrument; note the cause and corrective action in the inspection record.

Nonconformance handling
Identification
Any forging that fails to meet the requirements in the requirements table shall be segregated clearly and tagged as nonconforming. Establish a nonconformance tag linking the piece to its inspection record, heat lot, and the responsible inspector.

Disposition options
Disposition decisions include use-as-is, rework, scrap, or return to supplier as applicable under plant nonconformance procedures. Rework proposals must include method statements describing how the affected feature will be corrected without introducing new risks to functionality. For bore deviations, approved machining operations can be used to bring dimensions into tolerance if sufficient allowance exists and if the proposed correction is documented and approved by engineering prior to execution. For hardness deviations, submit a corrective heat-treatment plan and secure approval before proceeding. For weight deviations, investigate root cause and evaluate whether rework or scrap is appropriate.

Containment and corrective action
When a nonconformance is discovered that potentially affects previously released or in-process assemblies, apply immediate containment by locating all suspect parts, halting shipments if applicable, and notifying the quality manager. Document containment actions and propose corrective actions, including any changes to forging process controls, tooling, or inspection points. Maintain records of root cause analysis, corrective actions implemented, and verification of effectiveness.

Records to keep
Maintain the following records in the plant document control and quality records system for each heat lot and part number:
- Part inspection record containing individual hardness readings, bore measurements, and weight entries.
- Instrument calibration certificates or identifiers for the instruments used.
- Nonconformance tags and disposition reports where applicable.
- Engineering approvals for any rework or deviation requests.
- Traceability records linking the forging to the heat lot and manufacturing operations.

Examples and rationale
Example: A forging measures outside the bore tolerance at one axial station but within tolerance elsewhere. The inspector documents all measurements, segregates the part, and initiates an engineering review. If machining allowance exists, machining to size with appropriate quality controls may be approved. Rationale: Multiple-point measurement detects localized defects such as nonuniform cooling or die wear that single measurements could miss.

Example: Hardness readings show a regional trend toward the lower bound of the allowed range. The inspector increases sampling density and notifies heat-treatment personnel for process review. Rationale: Early detection prevents release of parts with out-of-spec hardness and limits rework.

Audit and review
Quality shall periodically review inspection records and nonconformance trends for CFW-6417-61 to determine ongoing process capability and identify opportunities for process control improvements. Maintain records as described for audit and continuous improvement purposes.
